# @forgesworn/fold-kit

> Circle primitives for private Nostr groups nobody operates: a room key per epoch, sealed to each device that stays; link invitations as capabilities; member removal by rekey; device credentials so a person approves a device once and it signs from then on. Extracted from KithMoot, byte-identical on the wire. Framework-free: owns no storage, UI, relay defaults or identity keys, and does no relay I/O of its own.

ESM-only, Node.js 22.13+. Two entry points: `@forgesworn/fold-kit` (everything) and `@forgesworn/fold-kit/lane` (relay lane classification only).

## Install

```bash
npm install @forgesworn/fold-kit
```

Not yet published to npm under this API. Until it is, pin an immutable Git commit:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@forgesworn/fold-kit": "github:forgesworn/fold-kit#<commit>"
  }
}
```

### Peer dependencies

`nostr-tools` (`>=2.24.2 <3`), `@noble/hashes` (`^1.8.0`), `@noble/curves` (`^2.0.1`) - peers, not dependencies, so a consumer keeps a single copy of each. `@noble/hashes` is 1.x only: this kit's imports have no `.js` suffix and its `hkdf` calls pass a string `info`, both of which 2.x rejects.

## Exports

### Identity, verification, hex

- `hexEquals(a, b)` → `boolean` - constant-shape hex comparison
- `normaliseHex(hex)` → `string` - lower-cases and validates hex
- `verifyEventUncached(event)` → `boolean`
- `boundedEventVerifier(limit?, verify?)` → `(event) => boolean` - an LRU-bounded verifier
- `localIdentity(participantSk)` → `ParticipantIdentity` - a local signer, plus the `ParticipantIdentity`/`UnsignedEvent` seam every codec below takes as a dependency

### Wire kinds and types

- `KINDS` → `{ CREDENTIAL: 20460, CHAT: 1460, INVITATION_REQUEST: 20466, INVITATION_GRANT: 20467, INVITATION_RETIREMENT: 1461, GROUP_INVITATION: 1463, ROOM_REKEY: 1462, EPOCH_REQUEST: 20468, EPOCH_GRANT: 20469 }`
- `DeviceCredential`, `AccessTier` (`'open' | 'ken' | 'kith' | 'kin'`), `AgentRule`, `RoomPolicy`, `KindredProof` - link-layer wire types
- `RelayTransport` → `{ publish(event), subscribe(filters, onEvent, onEose?), close() }` - the transport seam every relay-facing codec takes; this kit declares its own interface rather than importing a relay pool implementation

### Rooms, credentials, access

- `generateRoomSecret()` → `Uint8Array` (32 bytes)
- `deriveRoom(secret)` → `{ roomId, roomKey }`
- `encodeJoinUrl(base, secret, relays, policy?)` / `decodeJoinUrl(url)` - legacy v1 join URL
- `parseRoomPolicy(raw)` → `RoomPolicy | undefined`
- `createDeviceCredential(opts)` → `Promise<DeviceCredential>` - room-scope or person-scope (`scope: 'person'`)
- `verifyDeviceCredential(event, opts)` → `VerifyResult` - pass `acceptPerson: true` to accept a person-scope credential where a room credential is expected
- `PERSON_CREDENTIAL_MAX_SECONDS` - 30-day cap on a person-scope credential
- `RestampedCredentialExpiryError` - thrown by `createDeviceCredential` when a restamping signer would make a person-scope credential unverifiable everywhere; has `overBySeconds`; catch and retry with a shorter `expiresAt` margin (see CHANGELOG.md)
- `issueKindredProof(opts)` → `KindredProof`
- `evaluateAccess(policy, participant, proof, now, roomId)` → `{ admitted, reason }`
- `sanitiseDisplayName(raw)` → `string | undefined`, `MAX_DISPLAY_NAME_LENGTH`
- `safeRelayUrls(raw)`, `safeIceUrls(raw)`, `assertNetworkHintBounds(relays, ice)`, `MAX_RELAY_HINTS`, `MAX_ICE_HINTS`, `MAX_NETWORK_HINT_LENGTH`

### Links and invitations

- `parseRoomLink(url)` / `encodeRoomLink(base, link)` → `RoomLink` - the v1/v2/v3 link envelope
- `createRoomInvitation(persistent?)`, `roomInvitation(bearer, inviter, persistent?)`, `deriveInvitationId(invitation)`
- `encodeInvitationRequest(opts)` / `decodeInvitationRequest(event, opts)` - v2 live rendezvous request
- `encodeInvitationGrant(opts)` / `decodeRoomAdmissionGrant(event, opts)` - v2 grant, with a delegation chain
- `verifyInvitationDelegation(invitation, chain, now)`
- `encodeInvitationRetirement(opts)` / `decodeInvitationRetirementNotice(event, invitation)` - durable tombstone (kind 1461)
- `hostRoomInvitation(opts)` / `requestRoomAdmission(opts)` - the live desk, both sides
- Host `onGrantPublished(request)` / legacy `onAdmitted(device)` run after transport publication acknowledgement, not on approval. `onGrantFailed(request, error)` reports send failure; closed hosts suppress outstanding callbacks. Publication does not prove guest receipt or room entry.
- `encodePersistentInvitation(opts)` / `decodePersistentInvitation(event, invitation)` - v3 stored group invitation (kind 1463)
- `requestPersistentRoomAdmission(opts)` - joins from stored admission alone, no live desk needed
- Conference rooms: `encodePersistentInvitation({ ..., endsAt })` puts `ends` in the body and `['expiration', String(endsAt)]` on the 1463; `decodePersistentInvitation` returns `endsAt` and is null when an `expiration` tag disagrees with the body; `encodeInvitationRetirement({ ..., endsAt })` tags the 1461 the same way
- Room relays: `encodePersistentInvitation({ ..., relays })` puts the room's own relays (1-8 distinct canonical `wss://host/` URLs, else it throws) in the body after `ends`; the decoder returns `relays` and is null on a malformed list; `requestPersistentRoomAdmission` keeps the newest signed copy's list (a copy without one says nothing); `isInvitationRelays`, `requireInvitationRelays`, `MAX_INVITATION_RELAYS` (8)
- Self-destructing rooms (see `docs/room-destruct.md`): `encodePersistentInvitation({ ..., destruct: true })` puts `"destruct": true` in the encrypted body after `ends` (valid without `ends`), never a tag; `decodePersistentInvitation` returns `destruct: true` and is null when the field is present and not `true`; `requestPersistentRoomAdmission` keeps `destruct` if any valid copy carries it (sticky, like the earliest `ends`). `encodeInvitationRetirement({ ..., ended: true, destruct: true })` writes `{"v":1,"ended":true,"destruct":true}` (plain JSON, like `ended`) and throws on `destruct` without `ended`; `decodeInvitationRetirementNotice` returns `{ ended, destruct?: true }`, believing `destruct` only beside `ended`. `encodeRekeyEvent({ ..., closed: true, destruct: true })` writes it in the encrypted body after `closed` and throws without `closed`; `RekeyNotice.destruct` / `RekeyEvidence.destruct` are set only on a closing body, and a flag on an open rekey is dropped, not refused. Without the flag every event is byte-identical to 0.8.0, and a 0.8.0 reader ignores it
- `withExpiration(tags, expiresAt?)` - NIP-40 rule for a room that ends: add the tag, keep an earlier one, lower a later one; `isRoomEnds`, `requireRoomEnds(endsAt, now)`, `MAX_ROOM_ENDS_SECONDS` (30 days)
- Epoch encoders (`encodeRekeyEvent`, `encodeEpochRequest`, `encodeEpochGrant`) and `hostRoomEpoch` / `requestRoomEpoch` take `expiresAt?` for a conference room

### Epochs (removal by rekey)

- `deriveEpoch({ epoch, secret })` → `{ epoch, id, key }`, `generateEpochSecret()`
- `encodeRekeyEvent(opts)` / `peekRekeyEvent(event, opts)` / `decodeRekeyEvent(event, opts)` - the durable rekey notice (kind 1462), sealed per remaining device, naming who was removed
- `encodeEpochRequest(opts)` / `decodeEpochRequest(event, opts)` - a device asking the authority for the current epoch
- `encodeEpochGrant(opts)` / `decodeEpochGrant(event, opts)` - the authority's answer (secret, epoch-0, or a refusal `'removed' | 'closed'`)
- `epochRequestAdmission(opts)`, `deriveEpochRequestKey(roomKey)`
- `hostRoomEpoch(opts)` / `requestRoomEpoch(opts)` / `EpochRefusedError` - the live request/grant desk, both sides
- Member epoch catch-up (see `docs/member-epoch-catch-up.md`): `encodeRekeyEvent({ ..., commit: true })` writes `epochCommitment(roomId, epoch, secret)` into the rekey body; `hostMemberEpochDesk(opts)` lets any current member answer; `requestRoomEpoch({ ..., members: memberEpochSource(opts) })` asks the authority and members, first verifiable answer wins; `requestMemberEpoch(opts)` asks members alone. Kinds `MEMBER_EPOCH_KINDS` = `{ REQUEST: 20471, GRANT: 20472 }`. A member grant carries the authority-signed rekeys from the asker's epoch to the current one; the asker verifies the chain itself (`decodeMemberEpochGrant`) and refuses a last epoch with no commitment (legacy: authority only), a chain that removes it or closes the room, and one that stops short of `expected`. A verified grant is `{ epoch, removed, passed }`: `passed` holds the epochs between the asker's and `epoch`, oldest first, and `requestRoomEpoch` carries it as an optional `passed` when a member answered. Codecs: `encodeMemberEpochRequest`, `decodeMemberEpochRequest`, `encodeMemberEpochGrant`, `readRekeyEvidence`, `deriveMemberEpochRequestKey`, `MAX_MEMBER_EPOCH_CHAIN` (32)
- The known-members gate (#207, see `docs/member-epoch-catch-up.md`): once a room has removed anybody (`removed()` not empty), `hostRoomEpoch` and `hostMemberEpochDesk` grant only to a participant for which `known(participant)` is true; anybody else is reported through `onUnknown` (once per participant, and again every `reportUnknownEvery` seconds, default `REPORT_UNKNOWN_EVERY_SECONDS` = 60, while they keep asking) and refused: the authority answers `refused: 'unknown'` (an `EpochRefusal`), a member stays silent. `unknown` is not final: `requestRoomEpoch` keeps asking, calls its `onUnknown` once, and rejects with `EpochRefusedError('unknown')` only at its timeout; a desk looks at the requester's next ask afresh, so letting somebody in is making `known` say yes. No `known` after a removal means nobody is known. Member lists: `encodeRekeyEvent({ members })` writes the authority's list (removed dropped, sorted) into the body, read back as `RekeyNotice.members` and `RekeyEvidence.members`, and as `MemberEpochGrant.members` (newest in the chain); `hostRoomEpoch({ members })` puts it in its grants (`EpochGrant.members`). `readMemberList(raw)` reads one, undefined when malformed. Without `members` and with no removal every event is byte-identical to 0.5.1
- Seal keys (see `docs/seal-key.md`): `createDeviceCredential({ ..., seal })` appends `["seal", <x-only pubkey>]` last, under the participant's signature; mint a fresh one per credential with `generateSealKey()` and keep its secret as you keep the device key (old copies are sealed to old seal keys; healing needs only that each new one is fresh). `encodeRekeyEvent` recipients may be `{ device, credential }`; `encodeEpochGrant` and `encodeMemberEpochGrant` take `credential`; each copy is sealed to `sealTarget(device, credential)`: the credential's seal key, else the device key (never back to the device key because the credential lapsed). Readers take `sealSks` (`decodeRekeyEvent`, `decodeEpochGrant`, `decodeMemberEpochGrant`) or a `sealSks()` getter (`requestRoomEpoch`, `memberEpochSource`) and try them before the device key (`openSealed`); a rekey copy nothing opens reads as no copy. Desks take `credentialFor(device)`, the newest credential the room has seen (keep it monotone), and seal to the newer of that and the presented one (`sealCredential`, `newerCredential`: later expiration, then later created_at). `credentialSeal(c)` is the pubkey, undefined for none, null when doubled or off the curve (sealed to the device key). Without seal keys every event is byte-identical to 0.6.0
- Scheduled rekeys and the history window (see `docs/scheduled-rekey.md`): `encodeRekeyEvent({ ..., scheduled: true })` writes `"scheduled": true` inside the encrypted body (never a tag), and throws beside a non-empty `removed` or `closed`; `decodeRekeyEvent` (`RekeyNotice.scheduled`) and `readRekeyEvidence` (`RekeyEvidence.scheduled`) report `true` only when `removed` is empty and the room is not closed, so a contradictory body is still announced. `HISTORY_WINDOW_SECONDS` (30 days) and `MAX_HISTORY_EPOCHS` (16); `epochsInWindow(left, now)` keeps entries with `leftAt >= now - HISTORY_WINDOW_SECONDS`, newest first by epoch, first of a doubled epoch, at most 16, never throws. `encodeEpochGrant({ ..., passed })` takes `LeftEpoch[]` (`{ epoch, secret, leftAt }`) and writes `passed: [{ epoch, secret (base64url), left }]` oldest first, only when non-empty; it throws on more than 16, epoch 0 (the room secret is never carried), an epoch not below the granted one, a doubled epoch, a non-32-byte secret or a bad `leftAt`. `hostRoomEpoch({ past })` is asked on every grant, filtered to what the encoder accepts and to `epochsInWindow`, so a bad `past()` costs the history, not the grant. `decodeEpochGrant` returns `EpochGrant.passed` (`leftAt` set) only when the list is exactly in that form, else drops the field and keeps the grant; `decodeMemberEpochGrant` sets `leftAt` on each passed epoch from the next rekey's `created_at`. `MAX_MEMBER_EPOCH_CHAIN` (32) is a different limit. Without the marker and `passed` every event is byte-identical to 0.7.0, and a 0.7.0 reader ignores both
- `canonicalAdmins(admins)` / `signAdmins(opts)` / `verifyAdmins(opts)` - the authority's signed admin list
- `canonicalChannels(channels)` / `signChannels(opts)` / `verifyChannels(opts)` - the authority's signed channel list; `CHANNEL_NAME`, `RESERVED_CHANNELS`

### Scoped labels and sub-key certificates

- `deriveScoped(epoch, label)` → `{ id, key }` - HKDF from the epoch KEY under an app's own labelled namespace (e.g. `myapp/v1/board/<id>/update`); refuses this kit's own protocol namespace and any label outside `SCOPED_LABEL_PATTERN`
- `createSubKeyCertificate(opts)` → `Promise<DeviceCredential>` / `verifySubKeyCertificate(event, opts)` → result - a locally-signed, never-published statement binding an app-derived key to the credentialled device that minted it; `scope: 'sub'` is a value `verifyDeviceCredential` already refuses, so the two forms can never be confused. `verifySubKeyCertificate` takes `opts.credential` (the already-verified device credential) and reads its `device`/`expiration` tags itself; verification is strict (exactly four two-element tags, empty content) and canonical (expiration compared as the exact tag string). `SUB_KEY_CERTIFICATE_SCOPE`.

### Channel derivation

- `deriveChannel(roomId, roomKey, channel?)` → `{ id, key }` - a named channel's id/key, derived from the room key; `CHANNEL_ID_INFO`, `CHANNEL_KEY_INFO`, `MAX_CHANNEL_NAME_LENGTH`. The chat log and event codecs themselves stay in the consuming app.

### Lane (`@forgesworn/fold-kit/lane`)

- `laneOfRelayUrl(url, circle?)` / `laneOfRelays(urls, circle?)` → `Lane | undefined` (`'public' | 'sheltered' | 'direct'`)
- `isLane(value)`, `weakestLane(lanes)`, `isDowngrade(requested, actual)`
- `LANES`, `LANE_MEANING`, `LANE_LABEL`, `LANE_GLYPH`

## Design notes

- Every `kithmoot/v*` derivation label and message prefix is byte-identical to the source KithMoot commit this kit was extracted from (see EXTRACTION.md). These are protocol names now, not branding.
- No baked-in relay defaults, no storage, no DOM access. A caller supplies a `RelayTransport` implementation (a relay pool, or a test double).
- A room's authority - the party that may rekey and remove members - is the root inviter key pinned in the room's link, not a separate role system.

## Docs

- README.md - full API overview, peer dependency rationale, how this kit relates to `covey-kit` and `roost-kit`
- EXTRACTION.md - the source commit, exactly which modules and functions moved, and the two splits (`access.ts`, `chat.ts`) performed on the way
- AGENTS.md - build/test commands and repository conventions for an agent working in this repo

### Live persistent admission (opt-in codecs)

`parseLivePersistentEvent` bounds raw event JSON and refuses duplicate fields.
`encodeLivePersistentDescriptor` / `decodeLivePersistentDescriptor` carry
routing metadata alongside an unchanged persistent invitation link.
`encodeLivePersistentRequest` / `decodeLivePersistentRequest` and
`encodeLivePersistentAnswer` / `decodeLivePersistentAnswer` implement a fresh,
root-signed challenge/answer with no delegation. The answer retains epoch-zero
capability separately from `epochHint`. Constants bound request/answer lifetimes
to 90/30 seconds. `LIVE_PERSISTENT_ADMISSION_LABELS` freezes its distinct KDF.

These functions are codecs, not an offline join API. The host must have exclusive
durable lifecycle authority; the client must complete authenticated epoch
admission before publishing, including at epoch zero. No application enables
this profile automatically. See [the wire profile and integration gates](docs/live-persistent-admission.md).
Frozen synthetic fixtures are in `vectors/live-persistent-vectors.json`; run
`npm run build && npm run generate-live-persistent` to regenerate them.
